title: Smallest Window Containing All Letters

concept.title: Count what is still missing
body: You want the shortest block of `s` that contains every letter of `t` (with repeats: if `t` has two `a`, the block needs two). Keep a table `need` with the number of copies of each letter that the window still lacks (it goes negative for surplus letters) and a counter `missing` of the total number of letters still missing.

body.code:
for r, ch in enumerate(s):
    if need[ch] > 0: missing -= 1
    need[ch] -= 1
    while missing == 0:            # the window [l, r] contains all of t
        best = min(best, r - l + 1)
        need[s[l]] += 1
        if need[s[l]] > 0: missing += 1
        l += 1

body: The right end grows until the window is valid; then the left end shrinks as far as the window stays valid, recording every valid length on the way. Each end moves forward only, so the scan is O(n).

statement: Given two words `s` and `t`, find the shortest block of consecutive letters of `s` that contains every letter of `t`, counting repeated letters (if `t` has `a` twice, the block must have at least two `a`). If several blocks have the shortest length, print the one that starts first. If no block works, print -1.

examples.note: The shortest block with a, b and c is banc.

hints: Count how many copies of each letter of `t` are needed.
Move the right end forward; count a letter as found only if it was still needed.
When nothing is missing, record the window and move the left end forward while the window stays valid.

starter.python:
s = input().strip()
t = input().strip()

# Your code here

explanation: The window grows on the right until it covers `t`, then shrinks on the left while it still covers `t`. The shortest covering window seen, the first one on ties, is the answer.

code.python:
s = input().strip()
t = input().strip()

need = [0] * 26
for ch in t:
    need[ord(ch) - ord("a")] += 1
missing = len(t)
bestL, bestLen = 0, len(s) + 1
l = 0
for rr, ch in enumerate(s):
    c = ord(ch) - ord("a")
    if need[c] > 0:
        missing -= 1
    need[c] -= 1
    while missing == 0:
        if rr - l + 1 < bestLen:
            bestLen = rr - l + 1
            bestL = l
        d = ord(s[l]) - ord("a")
        need[d] += 1
        if need[d] > 0:
            missing += 1
        l += 1
print(s[bestL:bestL + bestLen] if bestLen <= len(s) else -1)
